insight: A top-level static import of an optional peer dep resolves at module LOAD, before any runtime enabled-gate can run — so gate optional-dependency imports dynamically inside the gated block, never at module top.

A flag named `--grade-yaml` set the field expectation that a YAML doc is accepted, but the writer read scores/decisions only from the markdown BODY — the fix is a normalizer that accepts both shapes, not a rename.
Two-file state split (tick.json vs reaction.json per repo) eliminated the COND-2 lost-update race by construction — separate writers never share a file, cheaper than merge-on-read keyed sections.
AC-3 happens-before ordering proven by reading state off disk INSIDE the spawn mock, not by asserting presence after the fact — the only test shape that survives refactors.
Prod ingest requires `emittedAt` ISO field and 422s without it; connect.mts still sends `timestamp` and fires its handshake without the bearer (401) — shape drift candidate FEAT.

Filesystem-lock polling budgets (80 attempts / ~2s) that pass in isolation blow up under full-suite load — same-process callers must serialize via an in-process promise-chain mutex; reserve the mkdir lock for genuine cross-process contention only.

Promise-chain mutex cleanup must compare the map entry against the caller's own promise object before deleting (get(key) === run) — otherwise a finished early link deletes a later caller's live chain entry.
prior.catch(() => {}) inside the chain link prevents one rejected update from poisoning subsequent same-key callers while each caller still observes its own rejection.
TTL steal tests that assert claimedAt is OVERWRITTEN (not merely present) are the only shape that catches a steal that forgets to re-stamp the claim.

Machine-wide caps need a single fleet-wide ledger file, not per-repo state — a correlated CI failure across N repos must trip one shared limit; compound keys (ghSlug::findingId) keep cross-repo entries disambiguated.
Every in-flight/claim style ledger entry needs a staleness TTL prune at read time (mirroring COND-1) so a crashed reaction can never permanently occupy a concurrency slot.
Gate-check reads must be read-only and never create the ledger file — assert this with an explicit never-creates-the-file test, not just a returns-zero test.
Sequential for+await sweeping plus the single-tick lockfile is what makes a lock-free gate read safe (stale-but-never-torn); if sweeping ever goes Promise.all, the gate needs a lock.

Platform branching belongs exclusively in the registration script; the tick entry point stays platform-neutral and a grep-assertion test (no process.platform in watch-tick.mts) pins that invariant permanently.

AC-8 no-divergent-code-path is provable cheaply by parsing both commands/watch.md and the scheduler script for the same watch-tick.mts entry-point reference, plus a unit test that main() delegates to runTick.
machineShard resolved from ~/.claude/watch/config.json (machine-level), not .claude/loop.json (repo-level) — shard identity spans repos; default keeps single-machine setups zero-config.
Committing slice-spec sharpening to main BEFORE cutting the worktree avoids the SLICE-145 spec-drift problem (worktree cut from a commit predating uncommitted spec edits).

Keeping arg construction a pure exported function in `reaction-spawn.mts` (spawn side-effect injected) let AC-3 be proven twice over: a unit test asserting `--dangerously-skip-permissions` never appears across every ReactionAction variant, plus a grep-style test over all spawn call sites in `src/scripts/lib/watch/` — no test ever spawns a real process.
Absent `allowedTools` machine config must degrade to Claude Code's normal permission prompts, never to a bypass flag — safe-by-default beats fail-closed-crash for an unattended tick.

Record-before-spawn with prune-on-failure closes the SLICE-145 crash window: a crash between spawn-resolve and ledger-record can no longer leak an untracked concurrency slot or double-spawn on the next tick (AC-3b test simulates the spawn failure and asserts ledger + claim state).

Per-entry try/catch in the sweep loop with a classified error kind (403/insufficient-scope vs 404/not-found vs other) makes "one dark repo" a recorded per-repo state instead of a whole-tick crash — the remaining shard keeps sweeping.

`lastSweepError { kind, message, at, consecutiveCount }` written through the existing atomic state path, cleared on the next successful sweep, bounds state growth: repeated failures bump a counter rather than appending an unbounded log.
Surfacing per-repo error counts in the tick envelope gives the dashboard a "repo went dark" signal without any new transport.

Dispatched agents emit bare idle_notification pings AFTER their report was already delivered and acknowledged (3 occurrences 2026-08-03: pm-scoring x2, reviewer-179 x1, all post-report and one post-closeout). Confirms FEAT-259 scope item 4 (idle-ping suppression) with live evidence independent of the original 2026-07-09 wave observation. Orchestrator must treat a bare idle ping from an agent whose report flag is set as noise and NOT re-nudge -- nudging a finished agent wastes a turn, and nudging a RUNNING one forks execution (dev-team#162).

Subagent review/validation artifacts written inside an isolated worktree land UNTRACKED at <worktree>/.claude/artifacts/... and are destroyed when the worktree is pruned. Confirmed SLICE-179: reviewer wrote its review-result there and git status showed it as '??'. Always copy (or commit) the artifact into the main tree before worktree cleanup, or the evidence chain for the close ceremony is lost.

Distinct failure mode from idle-without-report: a worktree builder can stop MID-EDIT with work uncommitted (SLICE-181, 2026-08-03 — HEAD still at main, 7 files modified, live exactOptionalPropertyTypes errors, final output a severed sentence). Worse than a missing report because an uncommitted worktree is DESTROYED on prune, losing the work entirely. FEAT-259's watchdog (slice 4) must detect 'stopped with uncommitted changes', not just 'idle without report' — and the recovery is a nudge to commit, not a respawn. Safe to nudge only because the agent was stopped, not running (never nudge a running builder; it forks execution per dev-team#162).

Worktree-isolated builders branch from committed HEAD, so they CANNOT see slice/FEAT files that are still untracked in the main tree. SLICE-181's builder correctly reported FEAT-276.md and its slice file 'do not exist anywhere' after checking all local+remote branches -- true from its vantage point, because every backlog artifact from that session was untracked in main. Commit backlog artifacts BEFORE dispatching any worktree builder, or the builder has no slice record to read ACs from or close against. Workaround that saved this run: the dispatch prompt restated the AC content inline, so the builder proceeded from the prompt plus astramem rather than blocking.
